html:
Germany occupied Luxembourg from May 1940 and treated it as part of the Reich, trying to wipe out its separate identity.

French was banned, French-sounding names were changed, and in 1942 young men were drafted into the German army. That set off a general strike, which was put down with executions. Thousands of Luxembourgers were sent to camps or to forced labour.

American troops freed the capital in September 1944, but the north was fought over again in the Battle of the Bulge that winter. The occupation, part of the Second World War, left Luxembourgers far more attached to their own language and state, and ended the country's faith in neutrality. Its ruler, Grand Duchess Charlotte, had spent the war in exile.
sum: Germany occupied Luxembourg from May 1940 and treated it as part of the Reich, trying to wipe out its separate identity.
